ladder.d.theta: Angle between ladder and floor; dragging the top along the wall changes it too
ladder.d.d: Distance of M from the foot, along the ladder; the climb starts here; dragging M changes it too
ladder.d.v: Speed of M along the ladder while it climbs
ladder.d.m: Mass of the uniform ladder; its centre of mass is at the middle
ladder.d.M: Mass of the person on the ladder (a point mass); 0 removes it
ladder.d.mu: Coefficient of static friction between floor and ladder foot
ladder.d.kr: Kinetic friction while the foot slides: μk = (μk/μs) × μs
ladder.d.crit: Show the ladder at the critical angle $\theta_c$ (dashed) and the critical position $d_c$
ladder.goal.cond: Two conditions for static equilibrium: net force $\sum\vec F = 0$ and net torque $\sum\vec\tau = 0$
ladder.goal.pivot: With the pivot at the foot, $N$ and $f$ exert no torque → the torque equation has a single unknown, $F_w$
ladder.goal.limit: Equilibrium holds only while the friction it needs, $f = F_w$, does not exceed the maximum static friction $\mu_s N$
ladder.goal.slip: Past the limit the ladder slips: Newton's second law for the ladder plus person, with kinetic friction $\mu_k N$ at the foot
ladder.obs.drag: Drag $M$ along the ladder; drag the top along the wall to change the angle
ladder.obs.climb: Play: $M$ climbs at speed $v$ → the lever arm $d\cos\theta$ of $Mg$ grows → $F_w$ and the needed friction grow; $N$ stays the same
ladder.obs.onset: At $d = d_c$ (time $t_s$) the gauge reaches 100 %: static friction is used up and the ladder starts to slip; the ▾ mark at 100 % stays
ladder.obs.slip: While slipping: $f = \mu_k N$ (gauge at $\mu_k/\mu_s$), $N$ below $(m+M)g$, $F_w$ falls to 0; tick on the floor = where the foot stood
ladder.obs.angle: A smaller angle lengthens the weights' lever arms and shortens that of $F_w$, $L\sin\theta$ → more friction needed
ladder.obs.crit: Dashed ladder = critical angle $\theta_c$ for the current $d$; bar across the ladder = critical position $d_c$
ladder.obs.over: Start position above $d_c$: the gauge passes 100 %, the friction arrow stops at $\mu_s N$ and the missing part is dashed; play → slips at once
ladder.obs.arms: Dimension lines below and to the left = lever arms about the foot: $(L/2)\cos\theta$, $d\cos\theta$, $L\sin\theta$
ladder.asm.wall: Frictionless wall → its force $F_w$ is horizontal. The floor exerts a normal force $N$ and friction $f$
ladder.asm.body: Uniform ladder (length $L$ = 5 m, centre of mass at the middle); the person is a point mass $M$ on the ladder at $d$; $g$ = 9.8 m/s²
ladder.asm.climb: $M$ climbs slowly at a steady speed (static analysis at every instant) and stops climbing when the slip starts: during the slip it stays at $d_c$, fixed to the ladder
ladder.asm.kinetic: During the slip the foot stays on the floor and slides away from the wall; kinetic friction $\mu_k N$ points toward the wall. Motion from Newton's laws (one variable $\theta$), RK4 step 1 ms
ladder.asm.wallleave: When $F_w$ reaches 0 the top leaves the wall (marker $F_w = 0$) and the ladder falls freely: that motion is not computed, the run stops there
ladder.asm.scale: Arrow length ∝ force (400 N = 1 m; all arrows shrink when the longest would exceed 2.2 m); playback speed 0.25× shows the slip slowly
